title: Axiomatic set theory: sets, classes, and the axioms of ZF
summary: The axioms justify familiar set constructions while excluding a set containing everything.
abstract: A description does not always define a set: allowing every possible collection leads to a contradiction. The axioms of set theory give precise rules that allow familiar constructions, such as subsets, pairs, and collections of function values, while ruling out a set containing everything. These rules provide a foundation for constructing numbers and maps from sets. Collections too large to be sets can still be described, but they cannot be treated as members of other sets.
